description: SocialCrawl credit guard: holds each paid API call's highest price, as it counts it, against a session limit when the command is a plain curl in the Bash tool, stays silent within it, and, once the vendor's free ledger shows a charge on an endpoint made while a call to it that finished cleanly was open, swaps that endpoint's finished holds for what was charged. The limit is the session budget in <revxl>/socialcrawl-budget.json when one is set (a whole number from 1 to 20,000), else min(500, 25% of the balance, rounded down), else 500 when the balance can't be read (not a number); a budget file that exists but can't be read or parsed, or a folder in its place, denies a call counted above 0 and never falls back to the automatic cap; a command that would take the session past it is denied, and reaching it exactly passes. Before such a refusal, when one of its counted calls has returned, it reads the free ledger once (at most once per 30 seconds) and settles returned holds first. It never raises a permission prompt: any other SocialCrawl command (not a plain curl, or through PowerShell) is denied with a message that names the fix, and so is every paid call in a session whose total was lost. Transcript calls, counted at one unit's price or their metered ceiling when that is higher (so one that bills many units is counted low), unreadable calls, counted at 50, and calls with a stated maximum (GET prism/investigate, POST web/sessions, GET economy/imports), counted at it, are refused past the limit and pass within the limit, transcript calls unless the person's transcript setting blocks them. Unpriced calls (cohorts) and calls with no stated ceiling (POST prism/jobs, POST web/batch-scrape, POST web/monitors), and the /v1/monitors calls (free to make, but each scheduled run then bills, unseen), are counted at 0, so the session limit does not stop them, even once it is used up. A call it can't record (no session lock before its wait ends, no session folder, a save that fails) is refused. Before a command, fires on Bash and PowerShell and only acts on socialcrawl.dev commands, but for one thing: it also guards its own files. A Write, Edit, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit of socialcrawl-budget.json, socialcrawl-day.json, credit-guard-unattended.jsonl or socialcrawl-calls.jsonl (or one of those names followed by a dot and more, such as a lock, temporary or rotated copy) in a revxl location (a folder of its path named revxl, or <revxl> itself), or of a session file or its lock in revxl/sessions/ or <revxl>/sessions/, or a Bash or PowerShell command naming one of them with a revxl location, is denied before anything else and is not logged (a command over 65,536 characters naming socialcrawl.dev is denied as not plain first, and logged when unattended); so is a Bash or PowerShell command that deletes, moves or renames the revxl folder itself (revxl or its sessions folder, the .claude folder above it, or <revxl>), and one naming budget-write, the save step behind the Save button in SocialCrawl → Settings; it refuses Claude running Save in any plain form, but a deliberately disguised command is not caught. The Read tool still reads them, and every other write-type call passes untouched. It keeps the session's count in <revxl>/sessions/ (SC_REVXL_HOME, else ~/.claude/revxl), and every wait it makes ends within 7 seconds of its start, under this hook's 10-second timeout. After commands, PostToolUse marks clean Bash returns and PostToolBatch reads free ledger sums to settle holds, silently within 4.3 seconds under a 5-second hook timeout. Each decision on a call it counts (a pass or deny made while it holds the session lock) adds one line, attended or not, to the call record <revxl>/socialcrawl-calls.jsonl: the time, session, paths, worst case, committed total, decision, kind, limit and the cached balance with when it was read, whether the run is a Desktop routine and the call's tool_use_id; a change the give-back makes to the total adds a settle line (decision settle, the total before and after); never a key or a command; at 1 MiB the record moves to socialcrawl-calls.jsonl.1, and a line that can't be written changes nothing. It reads the balance at most once a session (0 credits, at most 3 tries) when no session budget is set, logs each deny and paid pass made unattended or in a Desktop routine, and on an error of its own it refuses a command that mentions transcripts; other commands pass attended and are refused unattended or in a routine. Give-back limits: credits come back no sooner than about two minutes after a call returns, so the band can read high until then; a call that fails, is interrupted, runs in the background, or is piped or chained keeps its hold, and can count its hold and its charge together for the rest of the session; a finished call on an endpoint with no charge on the ledger this session (a cache hit, a free not-found answer) keeps its hold until one appears; nothing comes back without a key, or after three failed ledger reads in a row; other spending on the account on the same endpoint while a call is open counts against the session; and a charge the vendor records more than about 2 minutes after its call returns can be counted late, or not at all.
